subject: Contoso: Azure private marketplace listing & co-sell commercial terms
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Rios <procurement@contoso.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Contoso: Azure private marketplace listing & co-sell commercial terms

Hi Emily —

Thanks for taking the time on Friday. As discussed, Contoso is planning a private plan listing on Azure Marketplace and wants Redwood to be the listed vendor with a co-sell arrangement. Attaching a draft of the commercial terms & scope (Redwood_Azure_PrivatePlan_Terms_v3.pdf) to keep things moving.

Key asks we heard:
- Formal revenue share split for co-sell (MSCoS overlap)
- Payout cadence & invoicing flow (Contoso wants vendor invoice to Contoso, Contoso pays MS, or vice versa)
- SOW & support escalation responsibilities
- PO requirements and any special tax/withholding language

Can you confirm Contoso's preferred revenue split and whether procurement prefers Redwood to bill Contoso directly or for Contoso to facilitate through Microsoft? If you can share the PO template we can align legal redlines.

Next steps: I’ll loop in our legal (Laura) after you send the PO and any mandatory terms. If it helps, Marissa can join a brief call with the Azure Marketplace team to confirm listing mechanics.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0187

Attachment: Redwood_Azure_PrivatePlan_Terms_v3.pdf
From: Emily Rios <procurement@contoso.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <legal@contoso.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Contoso: Azure private marketplace listing & co-sell commercial terms

Hi Karthik —

Appreciate the doc. Quick answers from procurement/legal side:
1) Revenue split: Contoso is amenable to a standard co-sell model but needs a clear revenue-share waterfall. Our starting point is 70/30 (Contoso 70 / Redwood 30) net of marketplace fees. This is negotiable with strong justification for higher partner share.
2) Billing: Contoso requires vendor invoicing directly to Contoso (we want one invoice for subscription line items). Microsoft will handle marketplace registration and tracking.
3) Payment terms: Net 45 is preferred. Contoso cannot do Net 90.
4) Support & escalation: Contoso expects 24x5 support for production instances with an SLA escalation path — we’ll want contact names and a 4-hr P1 response window for critical incidents.
5) PO: attaching Contoso_PO_Template.pdf — please confirm acceptance or list redlines.

Samir (legal) — want to flag Contoso standard indemnity and data residency clauses; we’ll expect Redwood to accept Contoso’s model or propose commercial carve-outs.

If Redwood can accept the billing flow and Net 45, we can push to our vendor onboarding and Azure marketplace registration next week.

Thanks,
Emily Rios
Senior Procurement Manager, Contoso
Attachment: Contoso_PO_Template.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Rios <procurement@contoso.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Contoso: Azure private marketplace listing & co-sell commercial terms

Emily —

Thanks, that’s very clear and helpful. Quick confirmation from our side:
- Revenue split: Redwood can accept a 70/30 split if Contoso owns customer billing (i.e., Contoso invoices end customers and collects revenue). If Redwood is required to invoice Contoso directly, we would need a 60/40 split (Redwood 40) to offset marketplace commission and collection risk.
- Billing & payment: We can agree to vendor invoicing to Contoso and Net 45, provided tax and withholding are handled per the Contoso template.
- Support & SLA: Redwood commits to a 4-hr P1 response and 24x5 support as outlined; we’ll provide named escalation contacts in the SOW.

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura will circulate a redline of Contoso PO and the Azure marketplace checklist (Laura will send by tomorrow).
2) If Contoso is OK with the billing arrangement (Redwood invoices to Contoso / 70/30) we’ll prepare final SOW and DocuSign package.

Attaching an initial SOW draft (SOW_Redwood_Contoso_v1.docx) that maps support matrix and onboarding milestones.

Happy to hop on a short call today if useful.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: SOW_Redwood_Contoso_v1.docx
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <legal@contoso.com>, Emily Rios <procurement@contoso.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-13T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Contoso PO template - Redwood redlines

Folks —

Forwarding Redwood legal redlines to Contoso PO. Key commercial redlines we are proposing (see attached LAURA_redlines_Azure_terms_20261013.pdf):
- Payment & taxes: Redwood requests a clause clarifying gross-up for withholding taxes where applicable; otherwise Contoso to handle withholding and provide tax certificates.
- Indemnity: We propose limiting Redwood indemnity exposure for third-party IP to direct damages only, with a mutual carve-out for data-related claims.
- Data residency: Where Contoso requires EU/UK residency we will rely on Azure Private Plan configuration and provide SOC2 evidence.
- Liability cap: Redwood proposes liability cap at 3x the annual contract value or $5M, whichever is lower.

We tried to keep changes minimal to avoid procurement friction. If Contoso is comfortable with the billing flow and the 70/30 split with Contoso owning customer billing, these redlines should be acceptable.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
Attachment: LAURA_redlines_Azure_terms_20261013.pdf

Karthik / Emily —

Thanks for the thread. Quick checklist for private plan activation (Marketplace ID AM-PRV-2026-9982):
1) Confirm vendor billing model (Redwood invoices Contoso) — we see procurement has shared PO template.
2) Upload finalized commercial terms (Laura redlines accepted or countered).
3) Provide SOW and support contact list for the marketplace listing page.
4) Provide the Microsoft co-sell form and revenue share confirmation sheet (we’ll send a DocuSign envelope for the co-sell agreement).

We can schedule a validation call on Oct 15 to run through the listing metadata, co-sell wiring, and telemetry hooks.

Regard,
Azure Marketplace Private Plans Team
